rows.judge_notes: Buying then selling at the same stock level always loses coins (6% buy markup, 6% sell discount, symmetric stock-based pricing), and server-side validation and the game/HTTP/UI split are solid. Tests pass (12) but cover few server edge cases such as malformed JSON, and there are small flaws: a dead trailing `return;` in `nextDay`, and an oversized request body returns a 500 error. The UI is a decent game feel with sparklines, toasts and news, but it has no animation or clear price-trend cues.

rows.judge_notes: I found no money pump. Buys use a ceil'd price at mid+5% and sells a floor'd price at mid-5%, both walked unit by unit with 1% impact, so an instant round trip loses about 4% or more. The game logic is a pure module with 26 passing tests, and the server validates quantity, good and JSON and keeps all coins on the server; the UI is decent, with a news panel, price sparklines, a progress bar, a ledger and error toasts. It stops short of a full 2 because I only read the client code and did not run it in a browser, and its buy/sell buttons only offer quantities of 1 and 10.

I found no money pump. Prices rise as the market's stock falls, a 15% markup and 15% discount make every instant round trip lose coins, and the 21 tests pass, including random-trading checks. Game rules sit in a pure game.mjs, while the server owns all coins and validates quantity, goods and body size; the UI has sparklines, events and toasts, but it is a fairly standard card layout with no animation or sound.

I found no money pump. Prices fall as stock rises, and sales pay 85% of the buy price at the same stock level, so a round trip loses money. I checked this by reading the code and did not run a trade. The server validates goods, quantities and JSON, owns all state, and keeps the rules in a pure game.mjs. The 30 tests pass, and the UI gives clear feedback through toasts, a news feed, a ledger, price trends and live quotes.

All 29 tests pass. The game rules sit in lib/game.mjs apart from HTTP and UI. Every instant buy-then-sell round trip loses coins (+10% spread, 4% price impact per unit, rounding in the market's favor). The server validates inputs and holds all coin state, and prices react to trades and drift back over the days. The UI has clear state, toasts, a news log, an end screen and rent pressure. Minor nit: `handleApi` has a slightly awkward route-check block.

I read the game and server code by hand rather than running trade cycles against the API. By that reading, a same-day buy and sell round trip loses coins: a spread applies, each unit moves the price, and rounding never offsets the loss. All 33 tests pass, and the server checks goods, quantities, JSON and affordability, while game rules sit in a pure module. The UI has news, sparklines, trend arrows and trade feedback, but it greys out buttons without saying why and doesn't show net worth or rent during play.

rows.judge_notes: The game has a complete 30-day buy/sell/rent loop. Prices move with each unit traded, and a buy-then-sell round trip always loses money because of the spread and price impact. The server validates every input and enforces the rules, with the game rules kept apart from the HTTP layer. The suite is broad (58 tests) but one fails: the bankruptcy-over-HTTP test (api.test.mjs:274), which fails an assertion, so tests scores 1.

The rules in game.mjs are pure and separate from the HTTP layer. Every unit moves the price, a 5% spread applies, and daily limits, a reserve and rent are enforced, so I found no money pump in an instant round trip or in a next-day cycle. Validation is strict and all 65 tests pass. The UI is functional (price trend arrows, news events, quote preview, ledger, end-of-game screen) but is a plain card-and-button layout with no price history or richer game feel, so ux gets 1.

The economy is sound: an 8% spread, 3% price impact per unit and rounding against the player mean no instant round trip profits, and the server validates every input strictly. `node --test` ends at 57 of 58 passing, because the 100-parallel-buys test fails (4 trades succeeded where it expects 20, so it looks like a bad assumption or a flaky seed). The UI shows state, server quotes and errors, but gives little success feedback beyond the ledger.
